edits.headline: Nine killed during Kazakh naval exercise in Caspian Sea
edits.subheadline: Kazakhstan's Defence Ministry said 19 servicemen were swept out to sea and three were rescued, TASS reported.
editorialBody: Nine servicemen were killed during Kazakh naval exercises in the Caspian Sea, Kazakhstan's Defence Ministry said, TASS reported on 24 September.
The ministry said 19 servicemen were swept out to sea during the drills in Mangystau Region. Three were rescued and one was taken to hospital. A search for the others was continuing.
China confirmed that its first talks with the United States on artificial intelligence have taken place and hinted at an extension of the trade truce, CNBC reported.
Bitcoin fell below $83,000 on 24 September, CoinDesk reported. Traders priced in four Federal Reserve rate rises by June 2027, according to CME FedWatch data cited by CoinDesk.
A global bond sell-off deepened as oil climbed back to $105, the Financial Times reported.
Hong Kong authorities will not appeal a court ruling that halted a 12,000-flat housing project on a golf course, the South China Morning Post reported.
Saudi-backed forces in Yemen said they had repelled a Houthi advance on the Aden supply route, Middle East Eye reported.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told the UN General Assembly that the next secretary-general should be a Latin American woman, the Spanish government said.
